card.category: http tunnel over a wireguard link issued by curl
card.summary: SSL-terminated HTTP tunnels to your local machine - no custom software required, thanks to Wireguard

record.category: http tunnel over a wireguard link issued by curl

free_tier.stated: SSL-terminated HTTP tunnels to your local machine - no custom software required, thanks to Wireguard

egress.terms: No allowance or price is published; the page is four lines long.; ingress: http-only

record.chaining: Carries HTTP only; the WG link is the transport, not the ingress.
record.binding_note: Single-operator hobby tunnel. Ingress is restricted to HTTPS; raw TCP and UDP port forwarding to origin services are not supported.

identity_cost.detail: no account: the curl request is the whole signup.

record.reliability_note: One community host with no stated capacity or SLA.
record.confidence_note: The page sets no quota, so only a live transfer shows the real tolerance; the risk is that a shared community endpoint disappears.

evidence.proved: 'curl https://tunnel.pyjam.as/8080 > tunnel.conf && wg-quick up ./tunnel.conf'; 'You can now access ... on https://<unique_slug>.tunnel.pyjam.as/'

record.notes: The most interesting no-account entry in the sweep: a WireGuard config with zero registration, but the far side terminates HTTPS so the WireGuard link carries only HTTP. The same request shape would not forward a raw UDP port.

extras.wg_detail: The registration endpoint is the URL itself: 'curl https://tunnel.pyjam.as/8080 > tunnel.conf && wg-quick up ./tunnel.conf'. The port in the path is the local service, and the response is a wg-quick config.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance or price is published; the page is four lines long.
